reviews.comment: She is a great professor who is very knowledgeable. People complain because she is a bit coarse but if you treat her like a human being she will be great. She is a primatologist which is the most fun subject in anthropology!

The class wasn't hard, but it was a bit time consuming. Every week, there were two article prompts, two discussion questions, and a 10 question quiz only open on Sunday. There were no exams, and lectures were long but not difficult. There is a textbook, but you don't need it. Gurksy is nice and does a good job teaching and explaining everything.

The class is not hard at all, however if you skip you are basically screwed. A lot of the assignments are attendance based and its pretty much impossible to recover if you continuously skip. She was always nice to me but I think that's mostly because I participated in class.

Dr. Gursky is extremely knowledgeable and a top scholar in her field. The course is extremely easy YET interesting! You will want to engage with the material. Anyone saying she is rude probably doesn't actually pay attention or attend class because she was a peach all semester.

poorly put together lectures. disrespectful to students, commenting on their appearances and personal items. i would not take a course with her, and, quite frankly, the allegations against her are disturbing.

She kept discussions about worldview, but the homework, content, and PowerPoint were about cells. 
-Lectures would go too fast and only slow down to discuss "multi-gender" related topics
- Heavy workload she treats her class as your only class.


Lastly, I have a 3.8 GPA. if you also have a high GPA please DON'T take her class. it's not worth it.

Awful professor. Worst professor I've taken at A&M. She has a very limited emotional capacity and child-like tantrum when it comes to grades. She fails to outline directions for assignments and frantically sends emails to cover for every blunder she makes. Lectures are awfully put together. Quality of course is terrible.

Dr. Gursky is extremely rude and unwilling to work with your circumstances. My grandfather passed away and she literally did not care and did not give me time to complete my assignment. She also does not allow make up grades. Classes ended December 7th and grades were not due until the 15th. She just reads off slides and doesn't actually teach.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think she is a bit boring because she only read what she wrote on the slides show and recorded many lecture videos for us, you have no idea what questions she would give on the quiz; class itself is not very difficult, but you have to study very hard to get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was so confusing and hard for me. The tests etc are very hard to study for. She makes a final review but pretty much nothing from the review is on the final. There is not extra credit offered. She does however respond to emails quickly.

Weekly posts are very easy and manageable, only hard part are the weekly quizzes on lockdown browser. Only 2 exams. If you take bio 112 at the same time the material overlaps and is pretty easy. The final is very hard but multiple choice, and if you do good the entire year you can deal with a low grade on the final.
Bad lectures, tests are impossible, and I was bored most of the time and I was an anthropology major.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Gursky made this class so much harder than it needed to be. It was four tests and thats it. She gave us a reviews that were about 8 pages, which is fine but then the test was just solid trick questions. I learned the material but my grade did not reflect that. I did not feel like she wanted me to succeed.

Unless you can type extremely fast, you're better off just taking photos of the slides. Professor runs through them way too fast for anyone to be able to keep up, slides are never posted, review guides for the exams are useless, and the textbook readings aren't helpful. The exams are 75 questions and book is only used for little boxes. good luck
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am a Liberal Arts major and I took this class in order to fulfill a science credit requirement. Took this summer session I (5-week class) and it was a TON of work. Tests are HARD, even with notes. A lot of upper level material, boring (&LONG) lectures, HAVE TO take notes because PowerPoints not provided, no extra credit opportunities. Hated it.

Class is super interesting, and the tests are actually quite easy. You should show up since slides aren't posted online. There are boxes from the understanding anthropology sections in the textbook, but you can technically go to her office hours or her TA's office hours or the library and take pictures of the boxes before the exam.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The tests are 90% from in class lectures so show up. You will need the textbook to read these little boxes about anthropology so they're easy. 3 extra credit opportunities, very easy. 3 multiple choice exams with 70+ questions, and they've always been curved about 5 points. You can skip movie days since they're usually on media matrix.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes, lecture and note heavy but worth it. She's one of a kind and super interesting. definitely recommend!

Not the hardest class I have taken, but it's up there.  I took the online class which was pretty hectic.  A ton of power points combined with lectures, but again it was an online class.   You can make a higher grade than I did, but be sure if you take the online class do not take another class at the same time as I did.  Good Luck!

I'm very interested in anthro since I had already taken a anth class so I took this and my goodness, it was very hard for me. Tests covered so much little details, not possible to study enough. You do have extra credit opportunity (5 pts. Per test) and she did curve. Not sure about final though since I'm waiting for that grade still.

Dr. Gursky is not helpful at all. Her tests are hard and there is questions on the test that we had learned NOTHING about. She does ask questions about the "appreciating anthropology" sections in the book, so read those. Overall TERRIBLE!

She reads directly off the power point,yet still requires you to go to class. And when you are not experiencing story time, you are forced to watch movies that are 15-20 years old. The exams aren't to bad and it isn't hard to get an A,especially if you do the extra credit, but the class is extremely boring and not engaging at all.
Awesome lecturer, great experience and background. I loved her class!
